title: Add rare-token-sensitivity eval and CI soft-fail adapter
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduces a rare-token sensitivity smoke evaluation and a CI soft-fail adapter that flags regressions without aborting critical pipelines. Backwards-compatible; no runtime changes.
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent quality regressions that only surface when prompts include low-frequency or out-of-vocabulary tokens (typos, domain-specific identifiers, code tokens). Those regressions are high-severity for some customers but happen infrequently and previously caused noisy CI failures. This PR adds a lightweight "rare-token-sensitivity" (RTS) eval plus a CI soft-fail adapter which surfaces RTS regressions as flagged issues without immediately failing the entire CI pipeline unless thresholds are exceeded.

What this PR contains: 1) evals/rare_token_probe.py: generator that synthesizes prompt variants by injecting rare tokens, substitutions, and tokenization edge-cases across existing prompt-sets; 2) evals/metrics/rare_token_metric.py: computes an RTS-score that combines answer divergence, token-level hallucination increase, and semantic drift (cosine over embeddings) into a single normalized score; 3) ci/soft_fail_adapter.py: generic CI hook that converts configured eval severity bands into soft-fail vs hard-fail outcomes and posts annotated results to the CI job log and PR comments; 4) docs/rare-token-sensitivity.md: rationale, how to interpret RTS-score, recommended thresholds and remediation steps; 5) unit and integration tests plus a small historical backfill script to compute baseline RTS scores for existing prompt-sets so teams can adopt without blocking rollout.

Design notes and tradeoffs: - RTS-score is intentionally conservative in weighting: semantic drift and divergence receive higher weight than token-error counts to avoid surface-level noise. - The soft-fail adapter is pluggable; it is configured per-repo/pipeline via a YAML manifest with three bands (notice, soft-fail, hard-fail) and a minimum sample size. Default is to emit PR comments and fail the eval step only in hard-fail band. - No model-inference path changed; all changes are evaluation and CI-side. Backwards compatible with existing eval orchestration.

Checklist (all checked before merge): - [x] Unit tests for metric math and edge token cases (tests/test_rare_token_metric.py) - [x] Integration test exercising CI adapter behavior under simulated failures (tests/test_soft_fail_adapter.py) - [x] Documentation page with examples and recommended thresholds (docs/rare-token-sensitivity.md) - [x] Baseline backfill job that computes historical RTS per prompt-set and writes to /data/eval-baselines/rare_token/ - [x] Manual review from SRE for CI safety and rate limiting on baseline backfill

Testing and results: - Local unit test run: all pass (detailed in CI checks). - Integration evaluation on a sampled subset of 12 prompt-sets produced RTS-scores with mean 0.12 and std 0.04; three prompt-sets crossed the "notice" threshold and were triaged by authors. - Baseline backfill completed against last 90 days of stored evals; stored baselines included in release note artifacts.

Rollout plan: - Feature gate turned on for internal repos for two weeks (soft-fail band active) - After internal verification, flip notice->soft-fail thresholds for selected customer-facing pipelines - Expose per-prompt-set overrides in the Console (follow-up PR planned, LINK:ENG-4190)

Related: ENG-4128 (investigation into low-frequency token regressions), ENG-4190 (console feature to surface per-prompt overrides).

Notes for reviewers: I focused on keeping the metric deterministic and cheap (sampling-based) so it can run as a nightly eval or in lightweight CI. The adapter deliberately prefers visibility over hard gating until teams have baselines. Please pay attention to threshold defaults in docs/rare-token-sensitivity.md and the YAML schema for the CI adapter.
